feed.title: Vidhana — Sri Lankan IRD tax and VAT gazettes
feed.subtitle: What changed in the Sri Lankan Inland Revenue gazettes, and what the rule is now. Derived from https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/sitepages/gazette.aspx?menuid=1602

entry.title: 2500/106 [vat] amends 2481/22 and changes when it takes effect
entry.content:
As amended by Gazette 2500/106, the prescribed format and specifications for tax invoices issued by every registered person under the VAT Act apply from 1 October 2026, instead of 1 July 2026. All other requirements in Gazette 2481/22 remain unchanged.
Amends 2481/22 — The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from July 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax,.
This changes when 2481/22 takes effect. Check the date before acting on 2481/22 itself.
Effective from 2026-08-06.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2026_2500_106_E.pdf

entry.title: 2481/22 [vat] rescinds 2463/05
entry.content:
This notice requires every VAT-registered business to issue tax invoices using the specified format, including supplier and purchaser details, TINs, invoice numbering, supply details, VAT amounts and payment information. As amended by Gazette 2500/106, these requirements apply from October 1, 2026, rather than July 1, 2026; the earlier optional format under Gazette 2463/05 is rescinded from that amended effective date.
Rescinds 2463/05 — The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from January 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax..
The current document in this rule is now 2500/106 (2026-08-06).
Effective from 2026-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2026_2481-22_E.pdf

entry.title: 2463/05 [vat] new: The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from January 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax.
entry.content:
This gazette specified the tax-invoice format that every VAT-registered person was to use from 1 January 2026, including supplier and purchaser details, invoice numbering, supply information, VAT amounts, payment method, and record retention. As amended by Gazette 2481/22, these specifications were optional until 30 June 2026 and were rescinded from 1 July 2026; a replacement tax-invoice format applies from that date.
The current document in this rule is now 2500/106 (2026-08-06).
Effective from 2026-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2463-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2456/02 [vat] rescinds 1986/09
entry.content:
From 1 October 2025, VAT refunds for eligible exporters, project suppliers and approved projects will be processed under a new risk-based scheme replacing the former SVAT refund arrangements. Low- and medium-risk claims may be refunded without prior verification, while high-risk claims require verification first. Eligible businesses must keep their RAMIS details, bank information, schedules and supporting records accurate and provide information for checks; the gazette also sets October and November 2025 deadlines for closing outstanding SVAT transactions.
Rescinds 1986/09 — Specified the Guidelines to operate Simplified Value Added Tax Scheme that effective from 01.01.2016.
Effective from 2025-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2456-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2443/30 [vat] new: Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002, Procedure for Collecting and Paying Value Added Tax on the Supply of Services by a Non- resident Person through an Electronic Platform in Sri Lanka.
entry.content:
From 1 October 2025, VAT will apply to services supplied in Sri Lanka by non-resident persons through electronic platforms, including cloud services, streaming, online marketplaces, digital advertising and similar services. Non-resident suppliers must register when the stated turnover thresholds are exceeded, charge VAT at the applicable rate (currently 18%), remit it by the 20th of the following month, file quarterly returns and keep records. Consumers may see VAT charged on these services, while platform operators must exclude the value of goods or services supplied directly by the original supplier when calculating their own taxable service value.
Effective from 2025-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2443-30_E.pdf

entry.title: 2429/39 [stamp-duty] amends 1465/19
entry.content:
From 1 April 2025, stamp duty on instruments for leasing or hiring property is set at Rs. 20 for every Rs. 1,000 (or part) of the total amount payable over the lease or hire term, including any premium. If the term exceeds 20 years, the calculation is limited to the amount payable for the first 20 years. Hire-purchase agreements made under the Consumer Credit Act are charged Rs. 10 for every Rs. 1,000 (or part) of the total amount payable.
Amends 1465/19 — Stamp Duty Act - Order under Section 3 - Re. Stamp Duty for Affidavit, Policy of Insurance & etc..
Effective from 2025-04-01.
Affects: notaries; parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments.
Caution: this rule's history is incomplete — 2 referenced gazette(s) are not in the corpus, so a change made by a document we do not hold would not appear here. Check the gazette itself before relying on this.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2429-39_E.pdf

entry.title: 2414/14 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017, Regulations under Section 86 (7)
entry.content:
From 1 January 2025, withholding agents making payments outside Sri Lanka must withhold the applicable tax on payments to non-residents and obtain a Tax Clearance Certificate before remitting the money, unless the payment falls within the listed exemptions. The rules also require relevant payment details to be reported in withholding tax statements; banks and authorised dealers must collect remittance information and submit monthly schedules to Inland Revenue.
Effective from 2025-01-01.
Affects: income taxpayers; withholding agents.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2414-14_E.pdf

entry.title: 2378/33 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017, Notice under Subsection (3) of Section 145
entry.content:
The Commissioner General has specified that tax payments under the Inland Revenue Act must be made only by cash deposit, pay order or bank draft, or through the Online Tax Payments Platform (OTPP). This sets the permitted payment methods for affected tax payments.
Effective from 2024-04-04.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2378-33_E.pdf

entry.title: 2376/25 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, no. 24 of 2017, Regulation under Section 123 (8)
entry.content:
From 1 April 2024, the regulation requires specified government registries, government contracting officers, financial institutions and the Colombo Stock Exchange to regularly provide detailed information to the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. The information covers property and lease transactions, companies and shareholders, vehicles, government contracts, bank accounts and loans, and investments and securities transactions. The Commissioner General will separately notify each person or institution when its reporting must begin; information not previously maintained must be started from 1 July 2024.
Effective from 2024-04-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2024_2376-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2363/22 [vat] rescinds 2295/08 and amends 2282/26
entry.content:
From 1 January 2024, the VAT rate is 18% on imports and supplies of goods and on supplies of services, except for goods covered by paragraph 1(b)(a) of the earlier order. This amends Gazette 2282/26 and rescinds Gazette 2295/08 from the same date, so VAT-registered businesses must apply the revised rate to affected transactions.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
Rescinds 2295/08 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
Effective from 2024-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2363-22_E.pdf

entry.title: 2334/21 [income-tax] new: Notice made Under Section 102 of Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017
entry.content:
Additional classes of resident individuals must register under Section 102 of the Inland Revenue Act, unless they were already registered when this notice was issued. From 1 June 2023, this includes specified professionals, business registrants, certain vehicle and property owners, some employees, building-plan applicants, and individuals earning specified amounts from services in Sri Lanka; from 1 January 2024, it also covers individuals aged 18 or over who are not in Part A.
Effective from 2023-06-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2334-21_E.pdf

entry.title: 2316/13 [vat] rescinds 1868/10
entry.content:
From 1 October 2022, this order sets out how VAT on the supply of financial services must be calculated, including the treatment of profits, employee remuneration, economic depreciation, VAT and SSCL. Businesses must separately identify non-financial services where they keep certified separate accounts, or apportion value addition based on turnover, and submit specified accounts and schedules with the annual return. It rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 1868/10 with effect from the same date.
Rescinds 1868/10 — Order to specify matters relating to and the manner in which Tax is calculated in respect of VAT on Financial Services with effect from 01.01.2014.
Effective from 2022-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2316-13_E.pdf

entry.title: 2312/73 [stamp-duty] amends 1465/20
entry.content:
The order adds a new category to the stamp-duty schedule for leases of land within the Colombo Port City Economic Commission’s area of authority. It covers leases by the Commission where the lessee does not pay the lease premium, rent or other consideration in cash to the Government or the Commission, under an agreement to which the Government is a party; the treatment applies from the date the Port City Commission Act came into force.
Amends 1465/20 — Stamp Duty Act - Order under Sec. 5. Re. Affidavit & Mortgages by Public Officers.
Effective from 2022-12-31.
Affects: notaries; parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments.
Caution: this rule's history is incomplete — 2 referenced gazette(s) are not in the corpus, so a change made by a document we do not hold would not appear here. Check the gazette itself before relying on this.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2312-73_E.pdf

entry.title: 2312/16 [income-tax] new: Inland Revenue Act, no. 24 of 2017, Notice under Section 83A
entry.content:
From 1 January 2023, employers must withhold employment-income tax using different tax tables for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, multiple or secondary employments, and other specified payments. Employees with more than one employment must nominate a Primary Employment and provide declarations and, when changing jobs, previous withholding certificates. Employers must file annual employee payment and tax details, issue withholding certificates, and keep payroll and tax records for at least five years.
Effective from 2023-01-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2312-16_E.pdf

entry.title: 2310/20 [sscl] new: Return of Social Security Contribution Levy
entry.content:
The Commissioner General of Inland Revenue has specified the return form for Social Security Contribution Levy. Businesses liable for the levy must submit a completed return for each quarter beginning on or after 1 October 2022, by the 20th day of the month following that quarter. The form records monthly turnover, tax calculations and credits, and warns that penalties may apply for incorrect or late returns and non-payment.
Effective from 2022-12-14.
Affects: businesses liable to the Social Security Contribution Levy.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2310-20_E.pdf

entry.title: 2303/05 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/57
entry.content:
From 1 April 2022, financial institutions calculating banking-business profits may not deduct specific debt-claim provisions for the listed categories, including loans to associates, persons outside Sri Lanka and employees, or Stage 1 and Stage 2 credit facilities. They must maintain records of specific debt-claim provisions separately for Stage 1, 2 and 3 facilities using the prescribed format. This notice rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/57 from the same date.
Rescinds 2064/57 — Notice in relation to specific provision for a debt claim made by a person conducting a banking business.
Effective from 2022-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2303-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2300/25 [vat] amends 2282/26
entry.content:
From 7 October 2022, imports and domestic supplies of sanitary towels (pads) and tampons under H.S. Code 9619.00.10 are subject to VAT at 0%. The order also continues the VAT rates for specified imported goods listed in the schedule to Gazette Notification No. 2095/20.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-10-07.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2300-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2295/10 [betting-gaming] new: Regulations made under Section 4 of the Casino Business (Regulation) Act, No. 17 of 2010, read with Section 3
entry.content:
These regulations set the application and renewal process for casino licences, including a licence fee of Rs. 500 million for each five-year period and a 60-day application window for existing operators. Casino licence holders must appoint compliance officers, prevent unlawful conduct and entry by people under 21, keep specified financial and gaming records, prepare and audit annual accounts, and submit audited accounts to the Minister. The rules also allow licences to be refused, have conditions added, or be cancelled for non-compliance.
Effective from 2022-08-31.
Affects: casino licence holders and applicants.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2295-10_E.pdf

entry.title: 2295/09 [betting-gaming] new: Order under Section 2 of Casino Business (Regulation ) Act, No. 17 of 2010
entry.content:
The Order defines the specific area where a casino business may operate as the place or premises identified in the casino licence issued under the Act. It takes effect on 1 September 2022 and provides the location basis for licensed casino operations.
Effective from 2022-09-01.
Affects: casino licence holders and applicants.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2295-09_E.pdf

entry.title: 2295/08 [vat] amends 2282/26
entry.content:
This order set VAT on imports and supplies covered by subparagraph (b) at 15% from 1 September 2022. As amended by 2300/25 from 7 October 2022, subparagraph (a) also includes a 0% rate for imported or supplied sanitary towels (pads) and tampons; however, Gazette 2363/22 rescinded this order and replaced the subparagraph (b) rate with 18% from 1 January 2024.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-09-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2295-08_E.pdf

entry.title: 2282/26 [vat] amends 2151/52
entry.content:
This Order replaced the earlier VAT order and set VAT at 12% from 1 June 2022 for imports and supplies not covered by the specified imported-goods schedule. As amended by Gazette 2300/25, sanitary towels (pads) and tampons were made zero-rated from 7 October 2022; as amended by Gazette 2363/22, the general rate became 18% from 1 January 2024, and the 15% rate introduced by Gazette 2295/08 was rescinded.
Amends 2151/52 — Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-06-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2282-26_E.pdf

entry.title: 2258/18 [income-tax] new: Notice under Paragraph 10 of Sixth Schedule
entry.content:
This notice sets the method for calculating the local value added in goods and services for the additional deduction available for qualifying marketing and communication expenses. Businesses claiming that deduction must keep calculation worksheets, expense lists, supplier and associated-person details, contracts, and supporting invoices or tax invoices. It covers sellers of goods, manufacturers’ distributors undertaking marketing and communication, and service suppliers, including mixed or composite services.
Effective from 2021-12-14.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2258-18_E.pdf

entry.title: 2234/07 [vat] new: Information technology and enabled services prescribe for the purpose of item (Liv) of paragraph (b) of PART II of the First Schedule of the Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002 as amended by the Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, No. 9 of 2021
entry.content:
This Order, effective from 1 April 2021, identifies information technology and enabled services that qualify for the treatment under item (Liv) of the VAT Act’s First Schedule. Providers must meet conditions including a 70% local technical employee threshold for software-related services, at least 50% local value addition for most other listed services, and an exclusion for businesses created by splitting up an existing business. The underlying VAT treatment under item (Liv) is not reproduced in this Order.
Effective from 2021-04-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2234-07_E.pdf

entry.title: 2234/06 [income-tax] new: Information technology and enabled services prescribe for the purpose of Subparagraph (ii) of Paragraph (u) of Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 as amended by the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2021,
entry.content:
This Order prescribes information technology and enabled services for the tax treatment referred to in the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act, effective from 1 January 2020. Businesses providing the listed services must meet conditions including, from 1 April 2020, a minimum 70% share of local technical employees for specified software services, or at least 50% local value addition for other listed services; businesses formed by splitting an existing business do not qualify.
Effective from 2020-01-01.
Affects: employers; income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2234-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2232/06 [income-tax] new: Notice under Section 5,10, First Schedule and Third Schedule
entry.content:
This notice sets conditions for pension, provident, gratuity and savings funds approved by the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. An employer’s total contributions to terminal-benefit funds, including EPF and ETF, must not exceed 25% of its total salary bill for the accounting year; approved funds must also meet specified investment limits. EPF and ETF are treated as approved funds regardless of these conditions.
Effective from 2021-06-14.
Affects: employers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/IR_2021_2232-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2232/05 [income-tax] new: Guidelines under Section 57 of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2021
entry.content:
These guidelines explain how to calculate income tax for the 2019/2020 year of assessment after the 2021 amendments. Individuals must divide income and reliefs between the periods before and after 1 January 2020, while partnerships and other entities must apply the specified apportionment, tax rates, withholding-tax and tax-credit rules. Partnerships became liable for income tax on taxable income from 1 January 2020.
Effective from 2020-01-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2232-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2217/07 [income-tax] rescinds 2104/04
entry.content:
These regulations replace Gazette Extraordinary No. 2104/4 and apply from 1 April 2020. They require income taxpayers carrying out controlled transactions with associated enterprises to apply arm’s-length pricing and, where the stated thresholds apply, maintain transfer-pricing files, submit an annual disclosure form, and meet country-by-country reporting or notification requirements. They also set the recognised pricing methods, penalties for non-compliance, and rules for advance pricing agreements.
Rescinds 2104/04 — Regulations on Transfer Pricing.
Effective from 2020-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/TP_2021_ 2217-07_E.pdf

entry.title: 2194/50 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/63
entry.content:
This notice replaces Schedule 01 in Gazette 2064/63 and sets the requirements for registering an individual as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act. Applicants must generally be Sri Lankan citizens and residents aged at least 21, meet one of the listed professional or experience-based qualifications, and have none of the stated disqualifications. The Commissioner General may register or remove representatives and must publish the register at least once a year.
Rescinds 2064/63 — Notify the requirements to registered as Authorized Representative.
Effective from 2020-09-23.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2020_2194-50_E.pdf

entry.title: 2152/60 [vat] amends 2151/52
entry.content:
As amended by Gazette 2152/60, the 0% VAT rule in paragraph 1(a) of Gazette 2151/52 uses a specified earlier taxable period to calculate total inputs. It also defines locally sourced inputs as spending on locally produced agricultural, horticultural, fishing, animal husbandry or dairy products, and locally manufactured goods with at least 10% local value addition.
Amends 2151/52 — Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2019-12-06.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2152-60_E.pdf

entry.title: 2151/52 [vat] new: Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019
entry.content:
From 1 December 2019, VAT was set at 0% for qualifying services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses where at least 60% of inputs came from local sources; financial services were taxed at 15%, specified imports at their listed rates, and most other imports, goods and services at 8%. The local-input definitions were added by Gazette 2152/60. This position was later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2282/26 from 1 June 2022, which set the general rate for the covered imports, goods and services at 12%.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2019-12-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2151-52_E.pdf

entry.title: 2149/18 [stamp-duty] amends 1465/20
entry.content:
This Order added a new Schedule item covering instruments for leases of land by the Government, government representatives or the Urban Development Authority where the lease premium or rent is not paid in cash and the agreement involves the Government. The position was later amended by Gazette 2312/73, which also covers qualifying leases of land in the Colombo Port City area by the Colombo Port City Economic Commission, from the commencement of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act.
Amends 1465/20 — Stamp Duty Act - Order under Sec. 5. Re. Affidavit & Mortgages by Public Officers.
The current document in this rule is now 2312/73 (2022-12-31).
Effective from 2019-11-14.
Affects: notaries; parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments.
Caution: this rule's history is incomplete — 2 referenced gazette(s) are not in the corpus, so a change made by a document we do not hold would not appear here. Check the gazette itself before relying on this.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2149-18_E.pdf

entry.title: 2147/59 [vat] new: Order under Value Added Tax Act, to be Charged on Condominium Housing Units
entry.content:
From 1 November 2019, VAT is charged at 6% on services involving the supply of residential accommodation by selling a condominium housing unit. This affects businesses that make these supplies and may indirectly affect consumers through the price charged.
Effective from 2019-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2147-59_E.pdf

entry.title: 2130/02 [income-tax] rescinds 2064/54
entry.content:
This regulation replaces item (i) of the Schedule issued in Gazette 2064/54. The replacement covers income tax, super tax, surtax, or similar taxes paid in another country, while excluding any amount above the foreign tax credit allowed under sections 80 and 81 of the Inland Revenue Act. It applies from 1 April 2018.
Rescinds 2064/54 — Notification specify the taxes or other levies which the deductions shall not be made in calculating a person's income.
Effective from 2019-07-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2130-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2125/69 [vat] amends 2124/03
entry.content:
As amended by this Gazette, VAT is charged at 7% on services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound-tour services supplied by registered travel agents. This rate applies from 1 June 2019 to 31 March 2020 and replaces the order published as Gazette 2124/03 from 1 June 2019.
Amends 2124/03 — Value Added Tax Charged on Supply of Services by a Hotel, Travel Agent etc..
Effective from 2019-06-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2125-69_E.pdf

entry.title: 2124/03 [vat] new: Value Added Tax Charged on Supply of Services by a Hotel, Travel Agent etc.
entry.content:
This order imposed 5% VAT on specified services supplied by Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound tours supplied by registered travel agents, starting 21 May 2019. As amended by Gazette 2125/69, the 5% order was repealed from 1 June 2019 and replaced with a 7% rate for these services until 31 March 2020.
The current document in this rule is now 2125/69 (2019-06-01).
Effective from 2019-05-21.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2124-03_E.pdf

entry.title: 2104/05 [stamp-duty] rescinds 2091/03 and amends 1465/19
entry.content:
From 1 January 2019, this Order changed stamp duty on specified trade, business, profession and vocation licences: non-liquor licences are charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever is lower; most liquor licences are charged Rs. 20,000; and certain listed liquor licences are charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever is higher. As amended by Gazette 2429/39 from 1 April 2025, stamp duty also applies to leases and hire agreements at Rs. 20 per Rs. 1,000 of the total amount for the term, or Rs. 10 per Rs. 1,000 for qualifying hire-purchase agreements.
Amends 1465/19 — Stamp Duty Act - Order under Section 3 - Re. Stamp Duty for Affidavit, Policy of Insurance & etc..
Rescinds 2091/03 — Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 - Order under Section 3.
The current document in this rule is now 2429/39 (2025-03-27).
Effective from 2019-01-01.
Affects: parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments.
Caution: this rule's history is incomplete — 2 referenced gazette(s) are not in the corpus, so a change made by a document we do not hold would not appear here. Check the gazette itself before relying on this.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2104-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2104/04 [income-tax] rescinds 1823/05
entry.content:
These regulations introduced transfer pricing rules for transactions between associated enterprises, requiring them to use arm’s-length pricing and keep supporting records. Affected taxpayers also had to submit transfer pricing information with their income tax return, with additional documentation requirements for larger transactions and multinational groups. The rules in this gazette were later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2217/07, effective from 1 April 2020; the replacement applies for periods from that date.
Rescinds 1823/05 — Inland Revenue Act, No. 10 of 2006 - Transfer Pricing Regulations on International Transactions.
The current document in this rule is now 2217/07 (2021-03-02).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2104-04_E.pdf

entry.title: 2095/20 [vat] new: Order to declare that the Value Added Tax shall be charged on the importation of Woven Fabrics
entry.content:
VAT is set at 0% on the importation of the listed woven, knitted and related textile fabrics under the specified H.S. codes. This Order rescinds the earlier Order published as Gazette No. 2089/13 dated 17 September 2018, so importers should use this schedule for the covered goods.
Effective from 2018-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2095-20_E.pdf

entry.title: 2095/19 [vat] new: Order declare that the Value Added Tax shall be Charged on Wood Sawn or Chipped, Plywood etc.
entry.content:
VAT is charged at 5% on the supply or import of wood products under HS headings 4407 and 4408. This covers wood sawn, chipped, sliced or peeled to a thickness exceeding 6 mm, and specified veneering or plywood-related sheets over 6 mm thick.
Effective from 2018-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2095-19_E.pdf

entry.title: 2091/03 [stamp-duty] amends 1465/19
entry.content:
From 1 October 2018, item 04 stamp-duty rates for trade, business, professional and vocational licences were replaced: non-liquor licences were charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever was lower; most liquor licences Rs. 20,000; and specified arrack and bottled-toddy licences Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever was higher. Gazette 2091/03 was rescinded by Gazette 2104/05 with effect from 1 January 2019, which re-enacted these rates in a replacement item 04; this is the position as amended.
Amends 1465/19 — Stamp Duty Act - Order under Section 3 - Re. Stamp Duty for Affidavit, Policy of Insurance & etc..
The current document in this rule is now 2429/39 (2025-03-27).
Effective from 2018-10-01.
Affects: notaries; parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments.
Caution: this rule's history is incomplete — 2 referenced gazette(s) are not in the corpus, so a change made by a document we do not hold would not appear here. Check the gazette itself before relying on this.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2091-03_E.pdf

entry.title: 2089/13 [vat] new: Notify under value added tax act to charge on importation of woven Fabrics of silk, carded wool etc.
entry.content:
This Order imposes VAT at 5% on the importation of the listed textile and fabric products, identified by their H.S. codes. It covers a wide range of silk, wool, cotton, flax, synthetic and artificial-fibre fabrics, knitted fabrics, lace, coated fabrics and related textile products.
Effective from 2018-09-17.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2089-13_E.pdf

entry.title: 2089/01 [income-tax] amends 2064/53
entry.content:
This Order amends Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/53. It preserves the tax treatment promised in qualifying agreements entered into with the Board of Investment before April 2018: the enterprise’s profits and income, and dividends it pays, remain exempt or continue to be taxed using the agreed basis or rate under the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017.
Amends 2064/53 — Order under Sec. 194 of Inland Revenue Act, no 24 of 2017, that the Regulations of Transitional Provisions.
Effective from 2018-09-17.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2089-01_E.pdf

entry.title: 2088/25 [vat] new: Notify the Operation of Tourist Value Added Tax Refund Scheme (TVRS)
entry.content:
This Gazette sets out the Tourist Value Added Tax Refund Scheme (TVRS). Tourists may claim a refund of 80% of the VAT-exclusive value of eligible goods taken out of Sri Lanka, provided the purchases total at least Rs. 50,000 excluding VAT, are covered by no more than three invoices per day, and are made from an Authorized Retailer. Bottled water, aerated water, cooked meals, and goods that have been fully or partly consumed are excluded.
Effective from 2018-09-11.
Affects: consumers (indirectly, through prices); VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2088-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2088/02 [vat] new: Notify the operational date on section 58A of Value Added Tax Act
entry.content:
Section 58A of the Value Added Tax Act comes into operation on 11 September 2018. This gazette only sets the commencement date; it does not explain the requirements contained in section 58A.
Effective from 2018-09-10.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2088-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2078/06 [vat] new: Notify the Regulations for healthcare services for the purpose of Value Added Tax, w.e.f. 02.07.2018
entry.content:
From 2 July 2018, the cost of healthcare services other than hospital room charges is excluded when calculating the value of healthcare supplies for VAT. This replaces and rescinds the earlier healthcare-services order published in Gazette No. 1991/17 dated 1 November 2016.
Effective from 2018-07-02.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2078-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/64 [income-tax] new: Notify the fee to be charged in relation to an application for a private ruling requested by a tax payer.
entry.content:
A taxpayer requesting a private ruling from the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue must pay a fee of Rs. 25,000.00 for the application. The notice does not state a separate commencement date, so the fee applies as specified in this notice from its publication date context.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-64_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/63 [income-tax] new: Notify the requirements to registered as Authorized Representative
entry.content:
This notice sets the eligibility requirements for an individual to register as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act, including age, Sri Lankan residency and citizenship, specified tax or accounting qualifications, experience and fitness requirements. It also provides for registration, removal from the register and annual publication of registered representatives. The requirements in this notice were replaced by Gazette 2194/50 on 23 September 2020; as amended, the replacement schedule also recognises Chartered Tax Advisors and changes some qualification wording.
The current document in this rule is now 2194/50 (2020-09-23).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-63_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/60 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the withhold tax from payments where the payments made to any employee and rates of tax to be withheld from such payments.
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, employers must withhold income tax from employee payments using the applicable tax table for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, non-citizen employees, multiple or secondary employments, and tax paid by the employer on an employee’s behalf. Employers must also manage primary-employment declarations, issue withholding certificates, file annual employee and tax details, and keep relevant records for at least five years.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: employers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-60_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/59 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the Capital gain tax return and schedules to be furnished
entry.content:
People liable for Capital Gains Tax on investment assets realised on or after 1 April 2018 must submit the specified Capital Gain Tax return and schedules. The filing deadline is generally one month after the realisation; a separate rule applies when a resident individual’s total gains exceed Rs. 600,000, and joint ownership can require each resident individual to file. The prescribed forms are Annex I (Asmt_CGT_001_E) and Annex II (Asmt_CGT_002_E).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-59_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/58 [income-tax] new: Notice specify the circumstances under which a tax payer may designate an authorized representative
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, an income taxpayer may designate an authorized representative to communicate with the Inland Revenue Department in specified matters. These include registration and profile changes, tax returns, private rulings, reviews, refunds, extensions of time, investigations, capital gains tax returns, and any other matter specifically authorized in writing.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-58_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/57 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to specific provision for a debt claim made by a person conducting a banking business
entry.content:
The 2018 notice set limits on which provisions for debt claims a banking business could deduct when calculating taxable banking profits, including provisions for loans to associated persons or persons outside Sri Lanka. It was rescinded by Gazette 2303/05 with effect from 1 April 2022 and replaced by new specifications, which also exclude certain pawning, employee and multiple-facility claims and Stage 1 and Stage 2 impairment charges. The 2018 rule therefore no longer applies.
The current document in this rule is now 2303/05 (2022-10-25).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-57_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/56 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to the any period for which interest on a blended loan
entry.content:
This notice addresses the period used when interest on a blended loan is compounded. It says that another period recognised under generally accepted accounting principles is specified, but it does not identify that period in the document, so the practical calculation rule cannot be determined from this notice alone.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
(Summary confidence: low. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-56_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/55 [income-tax] new: Notice in relation to the circumstances in which losses on financial instruments
entry.content:
Losses on a financial instrument may be offset only against gains from the same type of financial instrument. This sets the required tax treatment for taxpayers reporting such financial instrument losses and gains.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-55_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/54 [income-tax] new: Notification specify the taxes or other levies which the deductions shall not be made in calculating a person's income
entry.content:
When calculating a person’s income, income taxpayers must not deduct the listed taxes and levies, including Economic Service Charge, certain taxes on financial services, Crop Insurance Levy, and specified levies under the Finance Act. Item (i) was later amended by Gazette 2130/02 to cover comparable income taxes paid in any country, subject to the foreign tax credit limitation, and applies from 1 April 2018.
The current document in this rule is now 2130/02 (2019-07-01).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-54_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/53 [income-tax] new: Order under Sec. 194 of Inland Revenue Act, no 24 of 2017, that the Regulations of Transitional Provisions
entry.content:
These transitional rules preserve certain tax exemptions, concessionary rates, losses, allowances, depreciation treatment, finance-lease calculations, approvals and notional tax credits when the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 replaced the earlier tax law from 1 April 2018. As amended by Gazette 2089/01 from 17 September 2018, qualifying enterprises with pre-April 2018 Board of Investment agreements may also continue their agreed exemptions or reduced rates for dividends paid by those enterprises.
The current document in this rule is now 2089/01 (2018-09-17).
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-53_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/52 [income-tax] new: Order under Inland Revenue Act, No 24 of 2017, (e) III of 3rd Schedule that the official emoluments of any individual who is employed by the Asian Development Bank.
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, official emoluments paid to an individual employed by the Asian Development Bank are treated as exempt amounts for the purposes of the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act. This means those emoluments are excluded from the relevant income-tax calculation.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-52_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/51 [income-tax] new: Order under Sec. 85 of Inland Revenue Act, No 24 of 2017, as being the Service's rendered with a Source in Sri Lanka and Pays to a resident Individual being
entry.content:
For section 85 of the Inland Revenue Act, these regulations prescribe categories of services treated as having a source in Sri Lanka when paid to a resident individual, including professional, construction, security, management, vocational and similar services. They also prescribe a 2% rate when a resident person makes a payment to a non-resident person. The regulations apply from 1 April 2018.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-51_E.pdf

entry.title: 2064/50 [income-tax] new: Deduction of Income Tax from Interest Payment to a Senior citizen on money deposite in Banks or Financial Institutions, From 01.04.2018
entry.content:
From 1 April 2018, banks and financial institutions must withhold income tax at 5% on a senior citizen’s interest income above Rs. 1,500,000 for the year of assessment. Senior citizens must submit a declaration each year for each account, stating whether the threshold is exceeded or the relief has already been used elsewhere; false or misleading declarations are treated as statements made to a tax official.
Effective from 2018-04-01.
Affects: income taxpayers; withholding agents.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2064-50_E.pdf

entry.title: 2042/21 [vat] new: Record Keeping Regulations No. 1 of 2017 under the Value Added Tax Act
entry.content:
These regulations replace the 1998 record-keeping rules and require every VAT-registered business to keep detailed, up-to-date records of taxable, exempt, excluded and suspended supplies, imports, purchases, adjustments and input/output tax. Businesses must maintain specified VAT control accounts, worksheets and schedules, submit the required schedules with VAT returns where applicable, and preserve records for five years after the relevant taxable period. The regulations also include special record and schedule requirements for RIPs, RISs and certain wholesale and retail businesses.
Effective from 2017-10-26.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2017_2042-21_E.pdf

entry.title: 2036/23 [esc] amends 1502/10, 1506/06, 1546/09
entry.content:
These regulations rescind and replace the earlier Economic Service Charge regulations published in Gazettes 1502/10, 1506/06 and 1546/09. They allow businesses in specified sectors to opt for prescribed quarterly turnover calculations, including special calculations for freight forwarders, certain exporters and primary dealers, and then calculate Economic Service Charge on that turnover. The document does not state a commencement or effective date.
Amends 1502/10 — Economic Service Charge Act.
Amends 1506/06 — Economic Service Charge Act - Amendment to gaz.Ex.No.1502/10 of 20.06.2007.
Amends 1546/09 — Economic Service Charge Act No. 13 of 2006 - Amendment to Gaz. Ex. No. 1506/6 of 18.06.2007.
Effective from 2017-09-13.
Affects: businesses liable to the Economic Service Charge.
